title: Quebec Premier and PM Carney discuss U.S. trade, homelessness at first meeting in Cambodia
summary: St-Pierre Plamondon said the meeting ended with federal support for the province's fight against homelessness, and the exchange of personal phone numbers. The premier also thanked the Prime Minister…

image.caption: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon joke around at the start of their first meeting in Phnom Penh, Cambodia on Sunday. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Montreal

St-Pierre Plamondon said the meeting ended with federal support for the province's fight against homelessness, and the exchange of personal phone numbers. The premier also thanked the Prime Minister for his support of an economic summit that will take place in Quebec in 2027.
The premier said that the tone was "very agreeable" and that the two leaders "had fun"

Prime Minister Mark Carney and Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon met for the first time since the provincial election at the Francophonie Summit in Cambodia — a 30-minute meeting that St-Pierre Plamondon called "very agreeable, very funny."
"From a personal standpoint, I think it went well," said St-Pierre Plamondon in a news conference following the meeting. "We laughed on several occasions, we had fun."
The two men met at a hotel in Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia, during the summit of the international body of French-speaking states and governments.
Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks at a summit event in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

The premier said that the meeting yielded tangible results, including federal support for the province's plan to tackle the homelessness crisis and the exchange of personal phone numbers to keep open lines of communication between the two.
The premier also celebrated Carney for helping to cement Quebec's deal to host an international economic summit in Quebec in 2027 that would help to diversify the province's trade.
He also said it was the first of many meetings they would have.

"What is evident for the two of us, I think, is that we share some of the same objectives," said Carney, emphasizing his desire to put an end to homelessness nationally and make life more affordable in all provinces.

St-Pierre Plamondon said that several issues were left outstanding that couldn't be tackled in their half hour meeting — namely: immigration, housing, the Alto high-speed rail project and a fulsome discussion on U.S. trade.
"We agreed that we needed to talk to each other on a regular basis," he said of how the province would collaborate with the federal government on U.S. relations.
"Historically, Quebec has been very active diplomatically in the U.S.. So we're going to do that."

When asked if the premier regretted the tone of his first interactions with the prime minister after being sworn in, where he accused Carney of muzzling him during an EU summit that took place in Montreal in October, St-Pierre Plamondon said: "I will never regret defending the interests of Quebec."

blocks.text: The premier said that over the course of the summit, he has been treated by and considered as a head of state with other countries which has led to meetings which yielded fruitful results for Quebec's economy.
"The truth is here, we are treated as a full nation," he said. "That recognition leads us to very practical conversations about what we can do from an economic standpoint."
He explained that bilateral meetings he has had at the generated commerce for the next years with countries who want to diversify their economic structures.
"In terms of a first visit abroad, we're very happy."
With files from the Canadian Press
